sections.title: The Majesty of God in Creation
observations: In this section, Job's friend Elihu speaks of the greatness of God as seen in the natural world. He emphasizes that God's voice is heard in the thunder and the storms, illustrating God's power and majesty. Elihu's description serves to remind Job of the vastness of God's creation and His sovereignty over it.

Elihu's focus on nature is significant as it reflects the biblical theme that creation itself declares the glory of God (Psalm 19:1). The awe-inspiring phenomena of the weather are not random but are under God's control, showcasing His omnipotence.

sections.title: God's Sovereignty in the Storm
observations: Elihu continues to describe the storm, emphasizing that it is a manifestation of God's power. He points out that God uses the storm to accomplish His purposes, whether for judgment or for mercy. This highlights the dual nature of God's actions in the world, where even calamity can serve a divine purpose.
This section challenges the reader to consider how they view adversity and natural disasters. Are they merely random events, or do they have a purpose in God's sovereign plan?

importantVerses.commentary: God thunders marvelously with His voice; He does great things which we cannot comprehend.
He causes it to come, whether for correction or for His land or for mercy.

questions: What does Elihu's description of God's power in nature teach us about our understanding of suffering and divine sovereignty?
How can we reconcile the idea of God using storms for both judgment and mercy in our own lives?
In what ways does the natural world reflect God's character and attributes?
